summary.text: One of Penelope's suitors in Apollodorus' catalogue of the fifty-seven wooers from Dulichium — also named among the wooers from Same in Epitome 7.29, distinct from Clymenus father of Eurydice at Pylos (Odyssey 3.450–495) and from Clymenus son of Oeneus (Bibliotheca 1.8.1).

story.text: Apollodorus names Clymenus among the suitors who devoured Odysseus' substance in the long catalogue of Epitome 7.27, listed after Hagius and before Philodemus.
The same name appears again among the wooers Apollodorus assigns to Same in Epitome 7.29 — one figure, or a namesake from another island, the Epitome does not say.
